probes.summary: Read-only topology and Kubernetes routing checks completed.
limitations: Initial VyOS wrapper and CNI discovery attempts were evaluator command-construction errors; corrected commands succeeded.

probes.summary: Evaluator DaemonSet, ClusterIP, DNS, cross-LAN HTTP, VyOS captures, and cleanup completed.
limitations: The initial evaluator DaemonSet needed a NoSchedule toleration for node2; it was corrected before testing.

probes.summary: Read-only operational-state audit completed across all nodes.
limitations: Historical bootstrap warning events were present, but current services and workloads were healthy with no active error journal entries.

assertions.summary: VyOS owns both LAN gateways; node2 is the Ready control plane and node3/node4 are Ready workers using LAN addresses and router host routes.

evidence.command: vbash -ic 'show interfaces; show ip route'
evidence.observation: eth1=10.100.211.254/24 and eth2=10.100.52.254/24; both LANs are directly connected.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf; kubectl get nodes -o wide; ip -4 -br addr; ip route; ps -ef | grep "[k]ubelet"'
evidence.observation: node2 is Ready/control-plane with Internal-IP 10.100.211.11; node3 and node4 are Ready workers with 10.100.52.11 and 10.100.52.12. node2 routes 10.100.52.0/24 via 10.100.211.254 and kube-apiserver/kubelet use 10.100.211.11.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'ip -4 -br addr; ip route; ps -ef | grep "[k]ubelet"'
sudo -H sh -c 'ip -4 -br addr; ip route; ps -ef | grep "[k]ubelet"'
sudo -H sh -c 'ls -la /etc/cni/net.d; sed -n "1,160p" /etc/cni/net.d/10-flannel.conflist'
evidence.observation: All Ubuntu nodes had the same Flannel CNI configuration; node routes included Flannel pod-network routes.

assertions.summary: Pods on every node communicated directly and through ClusterIP with working cluster DNS; Flannel VXLAN traffic was captured on both VyOS LAN interfaces.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'kubectl get pods -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs -l app=crosslan-http -o wide; kubectl get svc -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http -o wide; kubectl get endpointslice -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs -l kubernetes.io/service-name=crosslan-http -o wide'
evidence.observation: One Running evaluator pod was placed on node2, node3, and node4; ClusterIP was 10.104.184.130 with pod endpoints.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-rbhnr -- nslookup crosslan-http.eval-vyos-3tkbtcs.svc.cluster.local; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-rbhnr -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.244.1.4:8080/; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-rbhnr -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.244.2.3:8080/; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-rbhnr -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.104.184.130:80/; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-rbhnr -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://crosslan-http.eval-vyos-3tkbtcs.svc.cluster.local:80/'
evidence.observation: From the node2 pod, DNS resolved through 10.96.0.10; direct HTTP reached node3 and node4 pods; ClusterIP and DNS HTTP both returned successful node responses.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-2lj2b -- nslookup crosslan-http.eval-vyos-3tkbtcs.svc.cluster.local; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-2lj2b -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.244.0.5:8080/; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-2lj2b -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.104.184.130:80/; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-2lj2b -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://crosslan-http.eval-vyos-3tkbtcs.svc.cluster.local:80/'
evidence.observation: From the node3 pod, DNS, direct HTTP to node2, ClusterIP, and service-DNS HTTP all succeeded.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-xhvk9 -- nslookup crosslan-http.eval-vyos-3tkbtcs.svc.cluster.local; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-xhvk9 -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.244.0.5:8080/; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-xhvk9 -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.104.184.130:80/; kubectl exec -n eval-vyos-3tkbtcs crosslan-http-xhvk9 -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://crosslan-http.eval-vyos-3tkbtcs.svc.cluster.local:80/'
evidence.observation: From the node4 pod, DNS, direct HTTP to node2, ClusterIP, and service-DNS HTTP all succeeded.

evidence.command: sudo -n sh -c 'timeout 20 tcpdump -i eth1 -nn -c 8 "udp port 8472" > /tmp/eval-vyos-3tkbtcs-eth1.txt 2>&1 & timeout 20 tcpdump -i eth2 -nn -c 8 "udp port 8472" > /tmp/eval-vyos-3tkbtcs-eth2.txt 2>&1 &'
evidence.observation: Both eth1 and eth2 captured the same Flannel VXLAN/OTV flow: outer 10.100.211.11 to 10.100.52.11 and reverse, carrying inner HTTP between 10.244.0.5 and 10.244.1.4; 8 packets were captured on each interface.

assertions.summary: Required services, packages, CNI/runtime/certificate state, routes, saved VyOS configuration, and cluster resources were coherent; no duplicate, debug, credential-copy, temporary, or abandoned residue remained.

evidence.command: vbash -ic 'show interfaces; show ip route; show firewall; show nat source rules; show nat destination rules'; systemctl --failed; systemctl is-enabled ssh sshd; stat /config/config.boot; find /tmp /var/tmp /config -maxdepth 3 -type f ...
evidence.observation: No failed services or suspicious residue; SSH disabled; saved /config/config.boot exists; expected LAN routes and forward firewall state present; NAT is not configured.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'systemctl --failed; systemctl is-active kubelet containerd; systemctl is-enabled kubelet containerd; command -v kubeadm kubelet kubectl containerd; dpkg -l; systemctl list-unit-files; find /etc/kubernetes /etc/cni/net.d /var/lib/kubelet; ip route; ip rule; nft list ruleset; journalctl -u kubelet -u containerd -p err..alert; systemctl is-enabled ssh sshd; find /tmp /var/tmp /opt /root /home ...'
evidence.observation: kubelet and containerd were active and enabled; only expected Kubernetes/CNI/runtime commands, units, manifests, certificates, routes, and KUBE/FLANNEL nftables were present; no error journal entries, suspicious residue, or enabled SSH.

evidence.observation: Same coherent required state: active/enabled kubelet/containerd, expected Flannel/Kubernetes files and rules, no error journal entries, suspicious residue, or enabled SSH.

evidence.command: sudo -H sh -c 'kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl get pods -A -o wide; kubectl get daemonsets,deployments,statefulsets -A; kubectl get services -A; kubectl get namespaces'
evidence.observation: All nodes Ready; Flannel, kube-proxy, CoreDNS, and control-plane pods Running/available; only expected controllers, services, and namespaces remained; evaluator namespace was absent.

actions_performed: Completed all three authored probes in order.
Created only evaluator-owned Kubernetes workload and temporary VyOS capture files.
Deleted the evaluator namespace and confirmed pods, service, endpoints, DaemonSet, and capture files were absent.
Made no executor configuration changes and performed no reboot.
overall_summary: All three authored assertions passed. Harbor evidence collection was closed after live checks and cleanup.
